memory_candidates.content: Buffer-then-flush is the sanctioned pattern for any UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse hook that must durably record an event without dirtying a tracked file ahead of the command body's own precondition read: buffer to a self-ignored file inside an existing, already-gitignored directory, then drain it unconditionally from a Stop/SubagentStop hook (the one pipeline point guaranteed to run after the whole turn's command body and before the next turn's UserPromptSubmit). Preserve the audit guarantee by never special-casing an abandoned/revoked/expired record out of the buffer -- the minted-but-unused case is usually the forensically interesting one. Give the flushed event's top-level timestamp the real flush time and carry the true original moment in a detail.recorded_at field, rather than backdating.

To prove a verify-deploy.sh / run-all.sh suite failure is pre-existing rather than caused by your own uncommitted edit, swap in the pristine pre-your-commit copy of the one affected source file (git show <prior_commit>:<path> > the live path), re-run the single suite, and diff the result against your working-tree run; then restore the file and confirm git status --porcelain is clean. An identical failure on both copies proves the cause predates your change. verify-deploy.sh's TARGET argument must be the repo root, not a source-store subdirectory -- passing a subdirectory errors with 'no deploy tree ... nothing to verify'.
